title: Bluesky’s active user base is shrinking as its focus expands beyond the app
excerpt: Over a year following its post-election surge, Bluesky’s mobile app is seeing a continued decline in active users, though its remaining community is still relatively engaged.
content_html:
Decentralized social network Bluesky was one of the bigger beneficiaries of the exodus from Elon Musk’s X in November 2024, following the U.S. elections. But now, nearly two years later, the social network and would-be X competitor is struggling to hold on to its momentum.

According to data from digital intelligence provider Similarweb, Bluesky’s mobile app had 10.4 million monthly active users worldwide in June 2026, down 27.2% year-over-year. In addition, mobile daily active users continued to decline, falling 25.6% year-over-year in July to around 3 million.

These declines indicate that even though Bluesky’s app continues to add registered accounts, fewer people are using its mobile app on a regular basis. It also suggests that some of those who joined Bluesky due to their dissatisfaction with X post-elections haven’t stuck around long-term.

But the bigger takeaway here is not just that Bluesky’s post-election bump has shrunk. Bluesky’s app has lost more than half its monthly active users from its late-2024 high, which means that its app usage continued to shrink even after the initial post-election surge subsided. (Its quarterly average was around 22.1 million monthly active users in the fourth quarter of 2024, Similarweb’s data indicates, and it declined to 10.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. That’s a decline of around 52%.)

Building beyond Bluesky

While Bluesky’s numbers are down, those who stuck around are committed. Its smaller community remains relatively active, with a stickiness rate (the ratio of daily to monthly active users) of roughly 29% in June, about the same as Threads.

For Bluesky’s new CEO, Toni Schneider, these numbers may not be as concerning. The company is not entirely focused on making Bluesky (the app) succeed, but on making it possible for the underlying protocol (AT Proto) to power a growing number of social apps, services, and communities. That’s something that is now taking place, as projects like BlackSky and Eurosky are growing, while some AT Proto apps like the video-focused Skylight have found early traction, too.

In addition, the company has launched new products, like the AI-powered research tool Attie, and is now working on adding support for private data to Bluesky. The latter could generate new interest in Bluesky from a different type of user — those less interested in the public square, and more interested in private networking and communities.

What’s more, Similarweb’s data doesn’t necessarily suggest that Bluesky users have returned to X, as some may have feared.

Instead, the data shows that X’s worldwide monthly active users on mobile were down around 3% year-over-year in June, and X’s mobile daily active users dropped 7% in July to 123.7 million. (Of course, X remains a sizable social network with around 302 million monthly active users on its app as of June 2026 and a growing number of web visits, up 5.3% year-over-year in July to 4.7 billion.)

If anything, the app to now be concerned about is Threads. It’s unclear whether Threads is benefiting from Bluesky’s falling engagement, or if it has managed to attract a new set of people who had never used a Twitter-like service.

In any event, the Meta-owned app’s daily active users were up 21.3% year-over-year to 147 million in July 2026, and its website visits were up 112% year-over-year to 471.6 million.

Bluesky’s own public stats indicate the company now has nearly 46 million registered users, but it doesn’t share specific data on daily or monthly active usage.

content_html_zh:
去中心化社交网络 Bluesky 是 2024 年 11 月美国大选后埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 X 员工流失的最大受益者之一。 但现在，近两年后，这家社交网络和潜在的 X 竞争对手正在努力保持其势头。

根据数字情报提供商Similarweb的数据，2026年6月，Bluesky的移动应用在全球拥有1040万月活跃用户，同比下降27.2%。 此外，移动日活跃用户继续下降，7月份同比下降25.6%至300万左右。

这些下降表明，尽管 Bluesky 的应用程序继续增加注册帐户，但定期使用其移动应用程序的人数却在减少。 它还表明，一些因选举后对 X 不满而加入 Bluesky 的人并没有长期坚持下去。

但这里更大的收获不仅仅是蓝天在选举后的涨幅有所缩小。 Bluesky 的应用程序的月活跃用户数较 2024 年末的高点减少了一半以上，这意味着即使在选举后最初的激增消退后，其应用程序的使用量仍在继续萎缩。 （Similarweb 的数据显示，2024 年第四季度其季度平均月活跃用户数约为 2210 万，2026 年第二季度下降至 1070 万。 下降了约 52%。）

超越蓝天的建设

虽然 Bluesky 的人数有所下降，但留下来的人却很忠诚。 其较小的社区仍然相对活跃，6 月份的粘性率（日活跃用户与月活跃用户的比率）约为 29%，与 Threads 大致相同。

对于 Bluesky 的新任首席执行官托尼·施耐德 (Toni Schneider) 来说，这些数字可能并不那么令人担忧。 该公司并不完全专注于让 Bluesky（应用程序）取得成功，而是让底层协议（AT Proto）能够为越来越多的社交应用程序、服务和社区提供支持。 随着 BlackSky 和 ​​Eurosky 等项目的不断发展，这种情况正在发生，而一些 AT Proto 应用程序（例如专注于视频的 Skylight）也已经找到了早期的吸引力。

此外，该公司还推出了新产品，例如人工智能研究工具 Attie，目前正致力于为 Bluesky 添加对私人数据的支持。 后者可能会引起不同类型用户对 Bluesky 的新兴趣——这些用户对公共领域不太感兴趣，而对私人网络和社区更感兴趣。

更重要的是，Similarweb 的数据并不一定表明 Bluesky 用户已经返回 X，正如一些人可能担心的那样。

相反，数据显示，6 月份 X 的全球移动月活跃用户同比下降了 3% 左右，7 月份 X 的移动日活跃用户下降了 7%，至 1.237 亿。 （当然，X 仍然是一个规模较大的社交网络，截至 2026 年 6 月，其应用程序每月活跃用户约为 3.02 亿，网络访问量不断增长，7 月份同比增长 5.3% 至 47 亿。）

如果有的话，现在要关心的应用程序是 Threads。 目前还不清楚 Threads 是否从 Bluesky 参与度下降中受益，或者它是否成功吸引了一批从未使用过类似 Twitter 服务的新用户。

无论如何，到 2026 年 7 月，这款 Meta 旗下应用的日活跃用户同比增长 21.3%，达到 1.47 亿，网站访问量同比增长 112%，达到 4.716 亿。

Bluesky 自己的公开统计数据显示，该公司目前拥有近 4600 万注册用户，但它没有分享每日或每月活跃使用的具体数据。
